data.body_html:
Choosing between a Marbella yacht charter and a Malaga boat rental in 2029 comes down to budget, luxury level, and how far you want to travel to the open sea. Marbella’s fleet from Puerto Banús offers larger yachts, inclusive packages, and faster access to prime cruising spots. Malaga is cheaper but often requires extra fees for fuel, skipper, and drinks. This guide breaks down the key differences so you can book the right boat for your Costa del Sol holiday.

Price Comparison: Marbella vs Malaga

Marbella yacht charters start at €749 for 2 hours on an Astondoa 40 or Azimut 39, including skipper, fuel, drinks, snacks, insurance, and 21% VAT. An 8-hour day charter costs €2,299. Malaga boat rentals typically range from €300 to €600 for 2 hours, but these prices often exclude fuel (€50–€100 extra), skipper (€150–€200), and drinks. For a like-for-like 8-hour day, Malaga can reach €1,800–€2,200—close to Marbella’s all-inclusive rate. For larger yachts like the Mangusta 80 (€4,719 minimum 4 hours, jet ski included), Marbella has no direct Malaga equivalent.

Fleet Size and Luxury

Marbella’s fleet includes yachts up to 29 metres (Ferretti 94) and 24 metres (Mangusta 80), accommodating up to 12 guests. Malaga’s largest rentals rarely exceed 15 metres. If you want a flybridge, sundeck, or jet ski, Marbella delivers. Smaller boats like the Dubhe (8m, 5 pax) or Mariah SX21 (6.4m, 5 pax) are also available for budget-conscious groups.

Cruising Distance and Time to Open Sea

From Puerto Banús, you’re 10 minutes from the Mediterranean. Head east to Cala del Faro or west to Cala Cortés for swimming. Malaga’s marina sits inside a bay; it takes 30–40 minutes to clear the port and reach open water. That’s an extra hour of motoring on a half-day trip. Marbella’s proximity to Marbella Marina and Cabopino also means shorter travel to secluded coves.

Inclusions and Hidden Costs

Every Marbella charter includes a licensed skipper, fuel, water, soft drinks, beer, white wine, cava, light snacks, insurance, and safety equipment—plus Spanish IVA (21%). No surprises. Malaga rentals often list a base price, then add skipper fees, fuel surcharges, and catering. Always read the fine print. For most tourists, Marbella’s all-inclusive model is simpler and more predictable.

Local Attractions and Destinations

From Marbella, you can cruise to Estepona (15 NM west), Sotogrande (25 NM), or Gibraltar (35 NM). From Malaga, popular trips include Nerja (20 NM east) or Torremolinos (5 NM). Marbella’s coastline offers more variety: the Golden Mile, La Concha views, and exclusive beach clubs. Malaga’s city centre is vibrant but less yacht-oriented.

Parking and Accessibility

Puerto Banús has paid parking (€30–€50/day) and is accessible via the AP-7. Malaga Marina charges €15–€25/day. Both have public transport. If you’re staying in Marbella, chartering locally saves a 45-minute drive each way. If you’re based in Malaga city, renting locally is more convenient—but you’ll sacrifice yacht quality and inclusive service.

Which Should You Choose in 2029?

Choose Marbella if you want a luxury yacht, inclusive pricing, and quick access to open sea. Choose Malaga if you’re on a tight budget, don’t mind paying extras, and prefer a shorter drive from the city. For most visitors, the Marbella yacht charter experience delivers better value and less hassle. Browse our full fleet and book directly online.
